claims.statement: The WEEE Directive covers photovoltaic panels and promotes preparation for reuse, recycling, and recovery.

For used EEE shipments, EU rules require ownership or transfer documents, functionality-test evidence, item records, transport documentation, and protection against damage; absent proof, authorities may presume WEEE.
Demand hypothesis: scheduled, tested domestic lots will attract reuse buyers that reject anonymous removed panels.

contrary_evidence: New-panel price declines can erase the economic case for used modules.
Preparation-for-reuse remains a small share of WEEE recovery and testing cannot eliminate long-tail failure risk.

economics.acquisition_route: Demand hypothesis: the family renewable installer can validate one decommissioning workflow and recruit neighboring EPCs
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 100000 modules yearly at 45 PLN blended revenue yields 4.5m PLN; 20% EBITDA at a 6x data-marketplace value could exceed 5m PLN in 5-7 years
economics.founder_time: 15-20 hours weekly, with physical testing and transport delegated
economics.gross_margin_basis: Economics hypothesis: 55-70% after field test and serial-capture partners; platform does not own panels
economics.payback: Economics hypothesis: documenting 2000 modules at 45 PLN average recovers initial capital in 12-18 months before resale fees
economics.pricing: Economics hypothesis: 30-60 PLN per module for evidence and listing plus 4-7% of resale GMV
economics.retention_or_repeat: EPC portfolios generate scheduled repowering lots; buyers maintain standing performance and model requirements

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Installer-sourced provenance, module-level test history, realized degradation and resale data, and recurring buyer thresholds
fingerprint.customer: Commercial PV owners, EPCs, repowering contractors, second-life installers, refurbishers, and WEEE operators
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Pilot through renewable installers, then EPCs, asset managers, insurers, and preparation-for-reuse operators
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Owner mandate, forward decommissioning lots, serial capture, independent functionality tests, title packet, buyer reservation, and WEEE routing
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Owner or repowering contractor pays per documented module or lot and a transaction fee at transfer
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A site will repower but removed panels lack a trusted title, test record, buyer, and compliant fallback

structure.commercial_archetype: Owner-authorized second-life marketplace with evidence escrow
structure.control_point: Pre-removal title and provenance bound to a credible functionality test and scheduled lot
structure.critical_dependency: Used-module classification must be supportable; failed units need licensed WEEE handling with no hidden export

thesis: Solar owners and installers authorize future decommissioned-module lots; the exchange binds serials, provenance, functionality tests, ownership transfer, packing, and a BDO-qualified waste fallback. Demand hypothesis: credible used-versus-waste evidence and scheduled supply can unlock higher-value reuse before recycling.
title: PV Module Second-Life Title and Test Exchange
